newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power lower amid ample supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power lower amid ample supplies.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices fell further amid warm weather and abundant hydroelectric supplies, traders said Thursday.
"It's very warm and there is plenty of hydro," said one trader, adding the choice for generators of hydropower is to "spill or sell."

In the Northwest, temperatures were forecast to run 5 to 10 degrees F above normal through Saturday, moderating to 2 to 4 degrees above normal until early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
Southwest temperatures are expected to be slightly above normal through Friday, warming to 5 to 10 degrees above normal over the weekend.
Friday firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted at $11.00-12.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $13.00-14.00 for Thursday.
Off-peak COB was also lower at $5.00-7.00.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was down at $9.50-10.50, while off-peak was at $5.00-7.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was lower at $13.50-14.50, while off-peak was quoted at $7.00-8.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $13.00-14.00, while off-peak was at $6.50-7.50.
COB for second quarter delivery was quoted at $10.20-10.30 per MWh, down from $10.40-10.60 on Wednesday. PV for the second quarter was quoted at $13.90-14.10, down from $14.10-14.30.
Third-quarter COB was quoted at $16.10-16.40, with fourth-quarter at $18.00-18.30.
Third-quarter PV was quoted at $22.50-22.75, while fourth-quarter was quoted at $17.25-17.75.
